items.title: Generating a graded ring over its degree-zero part equals generating the positive part as an ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that homogeneous elements of positive degree generate a graded ring over its degree-zero part as an algebra exactly when they generate the positive-degree part as an ideal (statement lines 13998-14003). The proof does not compare the two filtered pieces abstractly: one direction reads polynomial generation without constant term, and the other inducts on the degree of a homogeneous element, writing it as a sum of multiples of the generators and using gradedness to replace each coefficient by its homogeneous component of the complementary degree before applying the induction hypothesis (proof lines 14005-14017). That degree bookkeeping on the coefficients is the substance, and the author writes it out. H2.
